entries.title: Romans 4:1
segments: What then shall we say that our father Abraham has found, according to flesh?

entries.title: Romans 4:2
segments: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has a boast; but not before God.

entries.title: Romans 4:3
segments: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness."

entries.title: Romans 4:4
segments: But to him working, the reward is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt.

entries.title: Romans 4:5
segments: But to him not working, but believing on Him justifying the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

entries.title: Romans 4:6
segments: Even as David also says of the blessedness of the man to whom God imputes righteousness without works,

entries.title: Romans 4:7
segments: [saying], "Blessed are those whose lawlessnesses are forgiven, and whose sins are covered;

entries.title: Romans 4:8
segments: blessed [is] the man to whom [the] Lord will in no way impute sin."

entries.title: Romans 4:9
segments: [Is] this blessedness then on the circumcision only, or on the uncircumcision also? For we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.

entries.title: Romans 4:10
segments: How then was it reckoned? Being in circumcision or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

entries.title: Romans 4:11
segments: And he received a sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith [while still] uncircumcised; so that he might be [the] father of all those believing through uncircumcision, for righteousness to be imputed to them also;

entries.title: Romans 4:12
segments: and a father of circumcision to those not of the circumcision only, but also to those walking by the steps of the faith of our father Abraham during uncircumcision.

entries.title: Romans 4:13
segments: For the promise that he should be the heir of the world [was] not to Abraham or to his seed through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith.

entries.title: Romans 4:14
segments: For if they of the Law [are] heirs, faith is made void and the promise is made of no effect;

entries.title: Romans 4:15
segments: because the Law works out wrath, for where no law is, [there is] no transgression.

entries.title: Romans 4:16
segments: Therefore [it is] of faith so that [it might be] according to grace; for the promise to be made sure to all the seed, not only to that which is of the Law, but to that also which is of [the] faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all

entries.title: Romans 4:17
segments: (as it has been written, "I have made you a father of many nations") --before God, whom he believed, who makes the dead live, and calls the things [which] do not exist as [though they] do exist.

entries.title: Romans 4:18
segments: [For he] who beyond hope believed on hope for him to become the father of many nations (according to that which was spoken, "So your seed shall be").

entries.title: Romans 4:19
segments: And not being weak in faith, he did not consider his own body already dead (being about a hundred years old) or the deadening of Sarah's womb.

entries.title: Romans 4:20
segments: He did not stagger at the promise of God through unbelief, but was strong in faith, giving glory to God,

entries.title: Romans 4:21
segments: and being fully persuaded that what God had promised, He was also able to perform.

entries.title: Romans 4:22
segments: And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.

entries.title: Romans 4:23
segments: Now it was not written for him alone that it was imputed to him,

entries.title: Romans 4:24
segments: but for us also to whom it is to be imputed, to the ones believing on Him who has raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead;

entries.title: Romans 4:25
segments: who was delivered because of our offenses and was raised for our justification.
